subject.title: [Feature]: Pattern-based channel allowlist for Discord (glob/wildcard support)

question: Should Discord allowlists gain an explicit pattern namespace, and what precedence should pattern matches have relative to exact channel, thread-parent, category, and literal `*` entries?
rationale: This changes security-sensitive authorization semantics and public configuration behavior; source inspection can establish the gap but cannot choose the intended policy or compatibility contract.

options.title: Add explicit patterns map
options.body: Introduce a dedicated Discord `patterns` config map with exact matches taking precedence, deterministic pattern ordering, safe glob semantics, and audit warnings for mutable-name authorization.

options.title: Interpret channel keys as globs
options.body: Treat metacharacters in the existing `channels` map as patterns, accepting a smaller schema change but risking reinterpretation of previously literal keys and less explicit security posture.

options.title: Keep exact keys only
options.body: Decline arbitrary patterns and direct dynamic workflows toward category inheritance or explicit channel management instead.

recommendation.title: Add explicit patterns map
recommendation.body: Introduce a dedicated Discord `patterns` config map with exact matches taking precedence, deterministic pattern ordering, safe glob semantics, and audit warnings for mutable-name authorization.

likelyOwner.reason: The shared matcher and recent Discord allowlist history make this the strongest available routing candidate for the authorization-policy decision.
